item.title: Fabregas: ‘Nico Paz a wonderful cocktail, Como players want Man City and Juventus’
item.description: Fabregas: ‘Nico Paz a wonderful cocktail, Como players want Man City and Juventus’ Cesc Fabregas hailed Nico Paz as ‘a wonderful cocktail’ of a football player, as the coach admits young players ‘don’t see Como as the apex of their careers, they want Manchester City or Juventus.’ The 22-year-old was a product of the Real Madrid youth academy and has flourished during his co-ownership deal with Como. That saw the Serie A club pay €60m to buy the other 50 per cent over the summer, giving Real Madrid an option to purchase him in June 2027 for €80m. Fabregas praise for Nico Paz TURIN, ITALY – OCTOBER 27: Cesc Fabregas, Manager of Como 1907, gives instructions to Nico Paz of Como 1907 during the Serie A match between Torino FC and Como 1907 at Stadio Olimpico Grande Torino on October 27, 2026 in Turin, Italy. (Photo by Valerio Pennicino/Getty Images) “Nico is physique and talent, vision and mentality,” said Fabregas in a press conference today. “He is a wonderful cocktail, his Mum and Dad did a great job. I used to play in his position, so I like talking to him, find out if he sees the same things I do. At times, I think players don’t even need to be coached on movement or control, it’s more about tactics. “The great thing about Nico Paz is he doesn’t think about it, he just does the right things.” There have been strong reports of a potential bidding war for Nico Paz in the summer, including Arsenal, Manchester United and more. COMO, ITALY – JANUARY 24: Como 1907 coach Cesc Fabregas issues instructions to his player Nico Paz of Como 1907 during the Serie A match between Como 1907 and Torino FC at Giuseppe Sinigaglia Stadium on January 24, 2026 in Como, Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images) Fabregas took the opportunity to muse on modern coaching methods and whether there is the risk of limiting the talent at the disposal of players. “Nowadays, we risk creating robots, which helps a certain type of player. However, with Nico Paz, knowing he can make the right choice to win or make the difference, that really helps. “This not thanks to my work. We just tried to push him on his mentality and consistency, but having a Number 10 that defends like he does, or a Number 9 like Tasos Douvikas who can help the defence, that’s special. “We are very happy with Nico Paz, and the credit all belongs to him.” MILAN, ITALY – APRIL 21: Nico Paz of Como 1907 talks to Cesc Fabregas, Head Coach of Como 1907 during the Coppa Italia Semi-Final match between FC Internazionale and Como at San Siro on April 21, 2026 in Milan, Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images) Fabregas has been able to develop many young players in his Como squad, who would’ve struggled for playing time elsewhere. Instead, they are featuring regularly in Serie A and the Champions League, gaining valuable experience. “A young player is like a sponge, he soaks up knowledge,” added the coach. item.description: Man United told to pay £50m to sign Premier League star in January Manchester United Monitor Calvin Bassey as Fulham Scramble to Secure New Deal Manchester United’s search for defensive reinforcements appears to be gathering pace, with TeamTalk reporting that Calvin Bassey has emerged as a serious option while Fulham fight to keep hold of one of their most important players. The Fulham captain has grown into a central figure at Craven Cottage, both in leadership terms and through his performances, and there is now a clear sense that his contract situation is becoming one of the more intriguing Premier League sub-plots ahead of the next transfer window. According to the report, Fulham are trying to tie Bassey down to fresh terms and are ready to improve his current salary significantly. However, the issue is straightforward enough. Their proposal is not yet at the level Manchester United could potentially offer, and that gap is giving this story real momentum. Calvin Bassey contract talks create opening Bassey, 26, is said to be central to Fulham’s plans. The report states that he has become the “undisputed leader of their defence” and that the club are working to reward his influence with a lucrative new contract. Even so, there is a notable complication in the structure of Fulham’s wage bill. As outlined in the report, “Formal negotiations have already opened with the player’s representatives, although discussions are proving complicated by Fulham’s existing wage structure.” That detail matters. Fulham are willing to go strong for Bassey, but there are internal limits to how far they can stretch. Photo IMAGO Bernd Leno remains their highest earner on more than £100,000 a week, and TeamTalk adds that “the terms currently offered to Bassey fall below Leno’s financial benchmark”. That leaves the situation delicately poised, particularly as “an agreement is not currently close”. Fulham do retain an element of control. The report explains that while Bassey’s initial deal is due to expire next summer, the club will trigger a 12-month extension, taking him through to at least 2028. In practical terms, that removes any immediate pressure to sell and gives the club leverage in negotiations, both with the player and any interested sides. Manchester United interest in Bassey becomes more concrete Manchester United have been linked with a number of defenders in recent months, and Bassey’s profile makes clear sense. item.title: Fan Gets Physical with Dončić After He Throws Wristband
item.description: Jayne Kamin-Oncea-Imagn Images Luka Dončić admitted he threw his wristband at a fan before getting shoved, a move that may have started a fight. The Lakers star lost his temper after his team blew a 20-point lead to lose 99-96 on Friday night. Blaming the fan for the push ignores the fact that Dončić tossed the item at a person first. That action was the spark, and the player needs to take full responsibility for it. The video from Amazon Prime Video shows the exact moment the trouble began. Dončić tossed his white wristband toward a woman sitting in the first row as he walked toward the tunnel. Reports note that the woman appeared to say something to him before he threw the gear. He then doubled back to grab the wristband, which led to the physical contact. Dončić explained the sequence in his own words after the game. “I just threw my wristband like I do almost every game, and then I heard she or he didn’t want it,” Dončić explained postgame, according to a report. He went on to describe the push that followed his attempt to retrieve the item. “So I went back to grab it, and he just pushed me, and then I gave it to somebody else.” While no one should touch a player, the NBA star created the volatile situation by treating a paying customer like trash. Throwing equipment at fans is never acceptable, regardless of the score. Luka Doncic involved in an incident walking off the court following game at Spurs: pic.twitter.com/920AalPX6O — Underdog NBA (@UnderdogNBA) November 28, 2026 The Collapse That Sparked the Temper The incident happened right after the San Antonio Spurs completed a stunning comeback to win the game. The Lakers held a 20-point lead before the third quarter, but the Spurs outscored them 30-14 in that period. The final score of 99-96 ended the Lakers’ run in the NBA Cup group play. This loss officially eliminated the team from the tournament, leaving them with a 2-2 record. Dončić finished the night with 31 points on 14-of-31 shooting, along with 8 assists and 6 rebounds. His frustration was clear, but his reaction to the fans was the real story. Security Steps In Immediately Lakers forward Jarred Vanderbilt pulled Dončić away from the fan after the shove occurred. Team and arena security moved in right away to separate the parties and calm the scene. The male fan who pushed Dončić was ejected from Frost Bank Center for his actions. Two-way big man Carson Cooper helped hold Vanderbilt back as the situation de-escalated. It remains unclear if the NBA will fine or suspend Dončić for his part in the exchange. The league will review the footage to decide on any punishment for the player. Throwing a wristband at a spectator may be a lapse in judgment that a star player cannot make. Dončić said he heard someone did not want the item, yet he chose to toss it at them anyway. That decision turned a routine postgame walk into a safety incident. item.title: Shannon Sharpe says one aspect of Joel Embiid’s game has become ‘awful’ now
item.description: Photo by Andy Lyons/Getty Images The Philadelphia 76ers may be one of the most in-form teams in the NBA right now, but Shannon Sharpe still isn’t overly happy with one area of Joel Embiid’s game. The 76ers most recently took to the court on Friday night, securing a 111-87 win over the Indiana Pacers to go 16-4 for the season. That result means they have a very comfortable lead at the top of the Eastern Conference, with no other side managing more than 12 wins at present. During that victory, Embiid scored 14 points, had 11 rebounds and three assists. But Sharpe is not happy with how the player is performing from three-point range. Shannon Sharpe calls out Joel Embiid’s three-point shooting Speaking on the Nightcap podcast after the 76ers beat the Pacers, he said: “The thing is, they have to keep Embiid, he’s a shell of himself Ocho. “He’s still a guy that can get you, like you said, 20 points. He can get you 10, 11 rebounds. But for whatever reason, he’s struggling from the field. “I mean, he’s just awful from three. He hit one tonight, but I think he’s shooting under 20% from three.” Embiid went 1-3 from three-point range on Friday and when looking at his overall record this season, it is hard to argue with Sharpe’s claim. Since first stepping into the NBA in the 2016/17 season, the Sixers star has a 33.4% three-point field goal average. Up until the current campaign, his worst return on that front came in 2024/25, which he ended with a 29.9% average. But in 15 appearances so far this season, he is managing around half of that total (15.6%). Embiid has already addressed his three-point shooting decline earlier this month, saying: “I think the way I’m jumping, and my hands [placement] are just not what it used to be. I just have to go back and look at the clips and see what we can change and get better.” Read more: Magic Johnson makes a prediction about the LA Lakers after narrow loss to Spurs Johnny Manziel breaks silence on fallout with LeBron James and his crew ‘World-class’: Erik Spoelstra gives ‘the greatest compliment you could give’ to one Knicks star

item.title: GB miss out on Davis Cup final as Alcaraz stars for Spain
item.description: Great Britain had not reached the final of the Davis Cup since they won the tournament in 2015 [Getty Images] Great Britain were unable to give Leon Smith the perfect send-off as Davis Cup captain as Carlos Alcaraz inspired Spain to a 2-0 victory in the semi-finals. Competing in their first Davis Cup semi-final since 2019, Britain fell short as Arthur Fery was unable to match the dazzling brilliance of Alcaraz, with the seven-time major winner surging to an emphatic 6-2 6-1 win. That was after rising star Rafael Jodar defeated Cameron Norrie 6-2 7-5 in the opening singles match to put Spain in the driving seat in Bologna. The defeat brings the curtain down on Smith's near 17-year tenure as captain, during which he led Britain to Davis Cup success in 2015. Spain captain David Ferrer, who is also stepping down after this year's tournament, will have the chance to guide his nation to their first Davis Cup title since 2019 when they face Italy in Sunday's final. Italy are the three-time defending champions, although they are without talisman and world number two Jannik Sinner because of injury. More to follow. item.title: Bronson Reed’s Wife: All About Paige Haley & Their Family
item.description: Bronson Reed and his wife, Paige Haley - Bronson Reed / Instagram The WWE has lost a tremendous talent. Bronson Reed , whose real name was Jermaine Haley, died on November 27, 2026, at the age of 38 due to “medical complications.” At the WWE Crown Jewel event just weeks before his death, Reed had suffered several broken ribs and a lacerated kidney. Following the shocking news, fans all across the world are mourning Reed’s death. When he wasn’t in the ring, Reed was a dedicated family man. He was married to Paige Haley, who is pregnant with their second child. Learn more about Reed’s life and family. How did Bronson Reed and Paige Haley meet? Reed and Haley were high school sweethearts in Australia and had been together a total of 24 years. At the time of Reed’s death, they were married. Back in 2020, Reed shared a throwback photo of his high school days with Haley. “She’s done more for me than she’ll ever know and everyone that meets her knows just how special she is. Forever my love,” he wrote about Haley. While her husband had a very public persona, Haley has preferred to stay out of the spotlight. Despite growing up in Australia, the couple’s home base was in the United States. “America is the land of opportunity. You see we guys come from overseas and come to places like WWE. That’s what America is all about,” Reed told TV Insider in 2024. How many kids do Bronson Reed and Paige Haley have? Reed and Haley’s daughter, Deja, was born in February 2024. Reed had been open about their difficulties in conceiving and how they’d undergone IVF. For Haley’s first Mother’s Day, Reed penned a beautiful note to her. “I watched this woman go to the ends of the earth to have our daughter Deja,” he wrote on Instagram . “She is truly the strongest person I know, and in this short time, she has already become an incredible mother. I know Deja is going to grow up proud to call you mum. Thank you, Paige, for giving me so much. For giving me reason and purpose. I love you.” View this post on Instagram A post shared by BRONSON REED (@bronsonishere) Related All About RJ Mitte's Fiancée Kennedy Suarez The wrestler was a proud girl dad, often sharing photos of little Deja on social media. On August 25, Reed posted a photo of himself carrying Deja. “Another year on this earth. Sometimes you need some mental clarity to always remember what matters most,” his message read. Earlier this year, Reed gushed over how excited he was to return home to his wife and daughter. “Finally heading home after a tour, is the best feeling. OMW to my girls,” he captioned a series of photos. When the WWE announced Reed’s death, the company revealed that Haley is pregnant with her and Reed’s second child. No further details were shared about Haley’s pregnancy. Read the latest entertainment news on TV Insider .

item.title: Red Sox Should Explore Signing 2020 Cy Young Winner This Offseason
item.description: Red Sox Should Explore Signing 2020 Cy Young Winner This Offseason originally appeared on NESN . Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Contending teams are always looking for pitching, and the Red Sox , despite having one of the best starting rotations in baseball, find themselves in a situation where making a move or two could make sense. The one thing the Red Sox have to be mindful of is not overspending on a starter, which is why taking a chance on a guy with above-average stuff who might not be what he once was could be a wise decision. Something similar to what the Red Sox did with Sonny Gray could make a lot of sense. Last offseason, the idea behind landing Gray was to add a veteran arm with a strong track record at a reasonable price. Shane Bieber is similar, as he's an arm who once had Cy Young-caliber stuff, and the hope is that he can get back to something close to that level. Bieber won a Cy Young Award back in 2020, posting a 1.63 ERA in 12 games during the shortened COVID season. Obviously, there's risk involved. Bieber has dealt with injuries, and it would be unfair to suggest that he's anything like he once was. However, that's exactly why he should be somewhat cheap. With Garrett Crochet, Payton Tolle, and Ranger Suarez, the Red Sox will have one of the best 1-2-3 punches in Major League Baseball next season, if not the best. If they could land a player like Bieber and he can do what he did in 2022 for the Guardians, when he posted a 2.88 ERA, they would undoubtedly have the best four-man rotation in the game. The question for Boston is how much it's willing to spend. There doesn't seem to be an expectation that Bieber will be too expensive, as he only threw 55.2 innings last season and 40.1 the year before. item.description: Aaron Rodgers gets free agency update after Steelers release that could end his career originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Pittsburgh Steelers lost to the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 11, and a few days later, after Aaron Rodgers went on The Pat McAfee Show to stir the pot with Mike McCarthy in particular, the Steelers waived the veteran quarterback. Rodgers hit waivers, but he went unclaimed. Now, he's a free agent and can sign with any team he wants this season. But there's one issue Rodgers now has to deal with: finding a team interested in his services. According to The Ringers' Tom Pelissero , there aren't any teams showing interest in Rodgers right now. If that doesn't change, with this 2026 season being Rodgers' last, his release by the Steelers could be what ends his Hall of Fame NFL career. Aaron Rodgers at risk of finding no new team after release from Steelers "No immediate suitors emerged for Aaron Rodgers after he cleared waivers Thursday," Pelissero reports. "And barring an injury-driven emergency, league sources don't foresee the four-time NFL MVP playing again in what Rodgers has repeatedly said is his final season." Coming into the 2026 NFL season, Rodgers made it known this would be his last year in the NFL. But after just 11 weeks, his season has been cut short, and not due to injury. He was waived by the Steelers following his public bashing of the Steelers' head coach, accusing him of sleeping during meetings and revealing the embarrassing "1, 2, 3, Packers !" breakdown from McCarthy at halftime vs. the Eagles. MORE : One play, two devastating injuries: How Aidan Hutchinson’s Drake Maye sack shakes up AFC, NFC playoff races While there's plenty of drama likely to come from the fallout between Rodgers and the Steelers, for the future Hall of Fame quarterback, what does his future entail? Unfortunately for Rodgers, it doesn't seem there is an interested team willing to call up Rodgers for a chance to start right now. It would have to be an injury to a quarterback on a contending team that has no other option but to turn to Rodgers. It might also take the backup struggling in a major way. A situation akin to what the Minnesota Vikings experienced, with Kyler Murray hurt and Carson Wentz playing horribly, led to a trade for Kirk Cousins. That's the kind of situation that might lead to the ex-Steelers QB finding a new landing spot this season. If he can't land with a new team, there's a real chance that Rodgers' career has ended thanks to his release from the Steelers prior to Week 12, a game in which the Steelers blew out the Denver Broncos 27-5 without Rodgers. item.title: Tom Pelissero Drops Major Update on Future of Aaron Rodgers
item.description: Has Aaron Rodgers already played his final NFL game? According to a new report from NFL insider Tom Pelissero, that appears to be a very real possibility following the four-time NFL MVP’s controversial departure from the Pittsburgh Steelers. Rodgers officially became a free agent Thursday after clearing waivers without being claimed . However, despite being available to sign with any team, the veteran quarterback apparently isn’t generating much interest around the league. Additionally, league sources believe it would likely take an injury to another quarterback for Rodgers to receive another opportunity. “No immediate suitors emerged for Aaron Rodgers after he cleared waivers Thursday,” Pelissero wrote on X . “And barring an injury-driven emergency, league sources don’t foresee the four-time NFL MVP playing again in what Rodgers has repeatedly said is his final season.” The report comes just days after Rodgers publicly unloaded on Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy during an appearance on The Pat McAfee Show . The quarterback was also absent from the Steelers’ facility Wednesday before Pittsburgh ultimately decided to release him. An Unceremonious Ending to a Legendary NFL Career? Rodgers’ situation has generated plenty of discussion around the NFL, including criticism from Tom Brady regarding the importance of keeping locker-room matters private. According to Reuters , Rodgers subsequently defended his decision to publicly criticize McCarthy. For Detroit Lions fans who spent nearly two decades watching Rodgers torment their favorite team as a member of the Green Bay Packers, it is difficult to imagine his career ending this way. The four-time MVP and Super Bowl XLV champion will eventually have his place in the Pro Football Hall of Fame, regardless of how his playing career concludes. Rodgers has not officially announced his retirement, and an injury elsewhere in the league could still change his circumstances. However, based on Pelissero’s latest reporting, there is a legitimate possibility that one of the greatest quarterbacks in NFL history has already taken his final snap.

item.title: Brad Faxon suggests Brooks Koepka actually has a ‘secret sauce’ with his putter just like Ben Crenshaw
item.description: Photo by Mike Ehrmann/Getty Images Brooks Koepka drafted in Brad Faxon to help him with his putting earlier this year. Koepka really struggled on the greens during the 2026 PGA Tour season, ranking well down in 121st in strokes gained putting. His woeful putting cost him the chance to win on the PGA Tour this year. There is absolutely no doubt about that. However, Brooks Koepka will be confident heading into the 2027 season as he continues to work closely with Brad Faxon . Interestingly, Faxon suggested he would love to help Koepka back in August of this year before the five-time major champion actually reached out to him. Now the 36-year-old will be hoping that Faxon’s influence helps him return to the winners’ circle. Brad Faxon suggests Brooks Koepka actually has a ‘secret sauce’ with his putter Faxon spoke about the work he has been doing with Koepka during The Skins Game on Friday. He responded when asked what his key message to the five-time major champion has been so far, as quoted by Golf Digest . “I think, really, if you ask what we have worked on, it’s, number one, get you back to enjoying putting again,” Faxon said. “That’s an important part that I think is really underrated. I think there’s a lot of great putting instructors out there that know tons about the putting stroke … When you have to read an instruction manual before you go out to play in something that’s meaningful, I think sometimes there’s too much of that that goes on. “And I just wanted him to kind of understand that his instinct was … you don’t get to the point Brooks Koepka has without having great instinct, athleticism and ability. “ Brooks Koepka’s ‘unique’ putting stroke Brad Faxon explained how Koepka’s unique putting stroke is something that actually gave him an edge over his rivals. “Brooks is unique,” Faxon explained. “His stroke … he never really aimed the ball right on the face directly. It was a little towards the toe. He had a little bit of a loop in his transition, a lot like Ben Crenshaw; Greg Norman even had that. And I’ve always told him that was what I thought was his secret sauce to how he became a great putter. “And I asked him if he would be willing to go back away from the mallet that he had been using for the last year or two and go back to his gamer. That’s the putter that he won his majors with, and I think he’s familiar with.” Ben Crenshaw is widely regarded as one of the best putters in the history of the game. So, if a ‘loopy’ putting stroke was good enough for him, it should be more than good enough for Koepka. If Koepka is able to take more of a natural approach to his putting, he will have a good chance of winning again. The American has to stop over-analyzing his putting stroke and remember what actually made him such a successful golfer in the first place.

The Padres have Freddy Fermin, Luis Campusano and Ethan Salas behind the plate and it is unlikely they carry all three catchers throughout the season. The free agent catching market is limited so it gives San Diego an opportunity to work a deal for other major league talent or minor league talent that will improve the farm system. The latter prospect could be ideal for a general manager like A.J. Preller who often makes moves to improve his club at the trade deadline. The Padres also have depth in the bullpen. Some of that dismissed with the expected departures of Jason Adam and Adrian Morejon, but the team currently has four left-handed relievers in Yuki Matsui, Kyle Hart, Wandy Peralta and the newly acquired JoJo Romero. Those four are joined by Jermaine Estrada, David Morgan, Jhony Brito, Bradgley Rodriguez and others who are players returning from injury or players who do not have defined roles because they were recently acquired or have been pitching in the minors. Of course Mason Miller anchors the backend as the closer. With that being said the catchers and bullpen pieces could be used to get talent from other clubs around the league. The New York Yankees are said to have interest in Freddy Fermin and Luis Campusano and clubs looking to add a reliable backup at the backstop position would be wise to reach out to the Padres. Bullpen arms are always a hot commodity at the trade deadline, but if another MLB team likes what they see from a San Diego reliever there is no reason to wait until the middle of the season, whenever that may be, to improve their roster while at the same time helping the Padres improve in their areas of need. San Diego has been quiet to this point on the free agent market and with minimal time remaining before the expected lockout on Dec. 1, the Padres need to do something to get better for the 2027 season — should there be a 2027 season. One way to get better without spending a ton of money is to use what pieces you have in the clubhouse and Preller and the front office should be open to making that happen should teams come calling. item.description: Nov 27, 2026; San Antonio, Texas, USA; San Antonio Spurs guard Dylan Harper (2) drives to the basket during Los Angeles Lakers guard Luka Doncic (77) during the first half at Frost Bank Center. Mandatory Credit: Scott Wachter-Imagn Images TPX IMAGES OF THE DAY Black Friday in San Antonio smelled like it did everywhere bargain hunters shopped–– like burnt coffee and cold parking lots. It also smelled like a 20-point lead souring. The Lakers left San Antonio with the stench of cheap gas station cologne –– losers in a 99-96 game that was theirs. The Spurs came out like the rest of the country after Thanksgiving: heavy, slow, not fully awake. They couldn't buy a basket. They turned it over like they were handing out leftovers. The Lakers looked like the team with the best record in the NBA. They walked in knowing it. The Lakers couldn't have asked for a better start –– up 20 at the half, holding San Antonio to 38 points. Victor Wembanyama was stuck in Walker Kessler's pocket, shooting through arms, only scoring eight and earning every one. Then the Lakers' lead got comfortable. That's the problem. A 20-point lead doesn't just relax a team; it puts it to sleep. The scoreboard says the game is over before it is; the body believes it first. For half the game, the Lakers were great. Luka Dončić had 14 in the first quarter and finished with 31 points, six rebounds and eight assists. He also had the worst 3-point shooting night of his career: 1-for-13 on 10 or more attempts. Dončić is shooting an abysmal 20% from deep over his last five games. A lesser player would've shrunk; he kept shooting. Kobe Bryant would've approved; it almost worked. Walker Kessler was the best part of the Lakers' night. He made Victor Wembanyama work for everything: 25 points on 25 shots, 16 rebounds, four steals and two blocks. That kind of work doesn't trend. "He took 25 shots and scored 25 points. Enough said," Redick said. He's right. Only a few people alive can make Wembanyama work that hard. Kessler did it on a night when nothing came easy for the Lakers. item.title: “That’s Ridiculous” – Martina Navratilova Pushes Back After Serena Williams’ Coach Questions Alexander Zverev’s No. 1 Ranking
item.description: Alexander Zverev © Imagn images Martina Navratilova recently backed Alexander Zverev amid criticism from Serena Williams’ coach Rennae Stubbs over his World No. 1 ranking. Stubbs questioned whether the German, who went 0-7 against Carlos Alcaraz and Jannik Sinner this year, deserved the top spot as the Italian and Spaniard missed significant tournaments. Stubbs’ remarks did not sit well with Navratilova. “That’s ridiculous,” Navratilova wrote on X. “There is no asterisk by the ranking- you can only play the people who are there. Zverev is #1- end of story.” Former Wimbledon doubles champion Paul McNamee also called out Stubbs for her comments. He pointed out that both he and Stubbs had reached World No. 1 in doubles, but that did not make them better players than Navratilova and McEnroe. McNamee reached World No. 1 on May 25, 1981, and held the spot for three weeks before being succeeded by John McEnroe. Stubbs also spent three weeks as World No. 1 in doubles. Zverev rose to World No. 1 on Nov. 2. He won the French Open and US Open titles this season, while Alcaraz and Sinner navigated lengthy injury absences. Alexander Zverev takes a dig at ATP chairman Andrea Gaudenzi over his comments about players using painkillers Alexander Zverev slammed ATP chairman Andrea Gaudenzi, who said current players are better at managing their physical condition and consume fewer painkillers than players did when he competed. Gaudenzi added that players in the past competed despite injuries while relying on painkillers. During a press conference ahead of the Davis Cup, Zverev called out Gaudenzi, saying that his remarks were unfair and that he had no idea how many painkillers players actually take. “It’s not like every time we take a painkiller we let him know,” Zverev said. “I think this year for me, it’s been a good year. I’ve said it before: I was much, much healthier this year than I was last year. Last year I was struggling a lot with my back. item.title: The Galaxy keep missing the playoffs. Fans want ownership to take action
item.description: Galaxy forward Kyogo Furuhashi reacts during a match against Seattle at Dignity Health Sports Park on Sept. 12. After winning the MLS Cup title in 2024, the Galaxy haven't returned to the playoffs. (Luiza Moraes / Getty Images) Statistically, it’s far easier to make the MLS playoffs than it is to miss them. Eighteen of 30 teams qualify for the postseason, meaning each one starts the season with a 60% chance of making the playoffs. No other major professional sports league in the U.S. is as generous. Yet the Galaxy failed to make the cut this year. And last year. In fact, the Galaxy have missed the playoffs four times in six years since Greg Vanney took over as manager. They also missed in three of the four seasons before Vanney arrived, meaning the Galaxy have cleared the lowest playoff bar in American sports just three times in the last decade. And they haven’t done it in consecutive seasons since Bruce Arena was the coach. Read more: Mauricio Pochettino's exit places U.S. men's soccer in a precarious state Arena left a decade ago. (To be fair, the last time the Galaxy did reach the playoffs, in 2024, Vanney guided them to a championship .) But wait, there’s more. Home attendance was down, dropping below the 20,000 per-game average for the first time in a non-COVID season since the Galaxy left the Rose Bowl for Carson in 2003. That’s a decrease of more than 18% since 2023. All this should be concerning for the team and its owners at AEG. The Galaxy, after all, used to be the model MLS franchise. It won the most games, had the best players, collected the most titles and led the league in attendance nine times. Today? Not so much. So does AEG have a plan to fix that? We reached out to Dan Beckerman , AEG’s president and chief executive, through a company spokesman, hoping for some clues. We never heard back. However, general manager Will Kuntz , speaking in a videoconference with the media Friday, agreed things are dismal. “I don’t think we did a good enough job collectively last year,” he said. “So for us, it’s really about taking a hard look at everything we’ve done process-wise and saying ‘hey, how can we be better?’ Because it cannot continue like this.” Galaxy coach Greg Vanney reacts during a match against LAFC at BMO Stadium on Oct. 25. (Luke Hales / Getty Images) Yet Kuntz, the architect of the MLS Cup team, may not be around to see that process through. Vanney still has two years left on his lucrative contract while Kuntz’s deal ends next month, so if there’s going to be a fall guy for the Galaxy’s recent failures, it’s likely to be the GM, not the coach. On Friday, Kuntz was already speaking of the team in the past tense. “I really enjoyed my time at the Galaxy. I love being here,” he said. “I’d like to be back if it was up to me. But it’s not.” Nor is it up to the team’s most loyal supporters, who would like to see someone sacrificed for the team’s fall from grace. item.title: How Columbus Crew turned it all around to set up MLS playoff showdown vs. Messi
item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. But he wasn’t the right fit for the Crew in the post-Nancy era. The Crew turned to Courtois, a former Crew academy and MLS Next Pro coach who continued the idea first expressed on the field so successfully by Nancy’s teams. The squad might not have been the entirely right squad, either. item.description: They came by car, by the special-event X80 bus, by bike if they were feeling sporty. They came in layers, in beanies and scarves, with Gotham’s black-and-sky-blue colors on top. They came on behalf of those who couldn’t come, capacity being reduced at this impromptu change of venue, each one trying to make noise for five. Gotham FC forward Sam Kerr (20) competes for the ball against Kansas City Current defender Gabrielle Robinson (24) on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026, in New York City. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect They came with some measure of outrage — these home-field shenanigans would never happen in men’s sports — while their better angels told them to come in joy, in celebration, everyone watching women’s sports. And then, 25 miles and 20,000 seats removed from their regular destination at New Jersey’s Sports Illustrated Stadium, huddled in the bleachers by a blue track ringing an immaculate pitch at Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island, in the shadow of the old Psychiatric Center and with the light fading over the Costco across the river, 5,000 devoted souls Sunday afternoon watched Gotham’s NWSL title defense end in a 2-1 semifinal loss to the Kansas City Current. “We lost today because we weren’t the better team,” Gotham winger and oracle Midge Purce said. “That being said, I would say it’s inexcusable. It’s not what you want in a professional league. It’s not what you want for women who are progressing in the United States and supposed to be one of the best leagues in the entire world. I think it’s a bad look for everyone involved. And we always want to be at Sports Illustrated in front of our fans when we earned that right throughout the season. But I would say it had no effect on performance today.” The match had been moved to Icahn on Monday due to concerns over the disintegrating field conditions at Sports Illustrated, which had unfortunately overshadowed Gotham’s quarterfinal victory there last weekend. Gotham was unbeaten in its past 13 matches at Sports Illustrated, which is operated by the Red Bulls of MLS. Croix Bethune, left, celebrates scoring a goal with Kansas City Current teammate Lo’eau LaBonta during an NWSL playoff match in New York, Nov. 15, 2026. Getty Images “I think that’s also part of the sadness,” head coach Juan Carlos Amorós said. “I think we never know what would have happened if we played on a good pitch. I think it was the right decision to come here. I think the pitch in the other stadium was unfortunately unplayable.” Tickets for the semifinal were reallotted and grabbed up in a hurry, while Gotham officials ground on the logistics of moving their game-day operations. “Obviously not ideal we had to change stadiums, but … I think that’s really awesome to come into a new environment, a new stadium, you have to adapt, you have to make sure you can bring that energy and our supporters did that tonight and that’s incredible,” Gotham midfielder Savannah McCaskill said. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.title: Gotham FC’s home semifinal moved to 5K-seat stadium in field quality debacle
item.description: Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. For the first time in franchise history, Gotham FC is set to host its semifinal match next weekend. But there’s an unfortunate twist. Gotham’s semifinal match against the Kansas City Current won’t be played at the club’s typical stomping grounds in Harrison, New Jersey. Instead, Gotham agreed to move Sunday’s match to Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island for better playing surface quality. “This was an extremely difficult decision, and one we did not take lightly,” Gotham president of soccer operations Yael Averbuch West said in a letter to fans. “After thoughtful consultation with coach Juan Carlos Amorós, our team captains, and our ownership, we felt it was important to prioritize a playing surface that appropriately allows our athletes to perform at their best. Providing our players with a high-quality surface to compete is a responsibility we take very seriously.” The Gotham FC starting eleven line up before the NWSL playoff quarterfinal in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. Lev Radin/Shutterstock Gotham is a tenant of Major League Soccer’s Red Bull New York at Sports Illustrated Stadium. The Red Bulls are scheduled to play an exhibition game there Saturday night, exacerbating concerns about the field quality. The state of Sports Illustrated Stadium’s pitch has been a cause for concern over the past two weeks. ESPN reported the NWSL fined Gotham $10,000 for poor field conditions during last week’s regular-season finale, after which the club was awarded its first league Shield. The pitch condition was once again a major sticking point after Gotham’s ugly quarterfinal win against the Seattle Reign. Retiring Reign midfielder Jess Fishlock called the field “atrocious.” Gotham defender Jess Carter was overheard saying the grounds were “so bad” when walking through the tunnel after the match. A week after Jaelin Howell injured her right ankle during a home game, the Gotham midfielder said the field was “pretty sandy” and “a little unstable.” Amorós acknowledged the rough conditions impacted the quality of the game. Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. Corey Sipkin for the NY POST “At this level, in this kind of game, as a league, and we should have a better surface,” Amorós said. “Unfortunately, our club and football club did absolutely everything in their power to make sure that was the case. Unfortunately, it wasn’t. But luckily, it looks like nobody got hurt, and the game was what it was.” It’s not immediately clear if the NWSL penalized Gotham for a second consecutive week because of the field. item.title: NYCFC fires head coach Pascal Jansen after second-half collapse
item.description: NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. New York City FC will be looking for a new head coach this offseason. Less than 24 hours after the club played its final match of the 2026 season, NYCFC announced that it fired head coach Pascal Jansen following a disappointing campaign that saw the club miss the playoffs for only the third time in its 12-year history. NYCFC went through an ugly 2026 season, finishing 11th in the Eastern Conference and being knocked out of playoff contention before the club even reached its Decision Day matchup with D.C. United on Saturday. The rough season was highlighted by the massive second-half collapse NYCFC went through following the World Cup break, posting a 5W-8D-6L record and sliding from eighth place to 11th. Jansen was informed of the decision by the club’s front office on Sunday morning and ultimately the decision to move on from him as head coach came down to the “failure of making playoffs” following a “disappointing season,” a source told The Post. NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. Getty Images The head coaching role will take on an even bigger role going into 2027 as NYCFC prepares for massive changes with the planned move into their new stadium and MLS changing their league calendar to a summer-through-spring format, which is in line with the European football calendar and includes an abbreviated sprint season that will run from February to May. The club views this next year as a “crucial point in franchise history” and the feeling is that NYCFC wants to make sure it has “the right leadership in place,” the source added. NYCFC will begin its search for a new head coach immediately, sporting director Todd Dunivant said in a statement released late Sunday morning. “We would like to thank Pascal for his commitment and contributions to New York City FC and wish him and his family all the best. This decision follows a thorough review of the season and reflects our ambition as an organization,” he said. One of the biggest problems that NYCFC faced this season – especially during its struggles in the second half – had been allowing late goals that would cost the club points, or matches altogether. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month.
